subject: Marketplace listing: timezone support windows & claim reconciliation
messages:
From: Sophie Clarke <sophie.clarke@acmecloud.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Azure Marketplace Compliance <azure-marketplace@microsoft.com>
Date: Fri, 9 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing - support hours / claims evidence request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for sending the draft listing. Azure compliance flagged two narrow items we need before we can move to co-sell enablement:

1) Support availability: your listing copy currently states "24/7 support with 1-hour P1 response". Can you provide the operational evidence for 24/7 coverage (on-call rota, escalation matrix) and clarify the SLA window across PST/UTC timezones? Our marketplace listing policy requires documented coverage across all target regions or an explicit regional carve-out.

2) Branding and claims reconciliation: there are three places where product copy references "enterprise-grade reliability" and "99.99% availability". We need a short explanation of the measurement window (monthly/annual) and any caveats (maintenance windows, scheduled downtime). If this is a contractual SLA vs marketing claim, please flag which is which.

We have a tight co-sell onboarding cadence — if we can get the evidence by EOD Monday (May 12) we can keep the listing in the upcoming regional launch wave.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Clarke
Partner Programs, Acme Cloud Services

Tessa — sent the initial matrices. See attached: sla-support-window-matrix.csv (shift table showing PST/UTC coverage), and acme_evidence_matrix.xlsx (evidence map linking support runbooks, on-call policies, and escalation contacts).

Notes on coverage:
- We operate a primary NOC in PST with follow-the-sun escalation into our EU night team. Raw on-call roster is included; primary P1 triage is handled within 60 minutes 24/7. Secondary escalation may be outside 60 minutes during cross-team handoffs for uncommon specialty issues — those are documented in the escalation matrix.
- We recommend wording in the listing: "24/7 triage with 1-hour initial response for critical incidents; escalation timelines apply for specialized remediation." That keeps the marketplace claim factual without committing to contractual repair SLAs.

Laura — flagging the last point for legal review: do we want to expose the 99.99% figure as a contractual statement or keep as marketing? If contractual, we need to confirm measurement window and remedy terms.

Ben

Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing - support hours / claims evidence request

Hi Sophie — thanks for the details and the deadline callout. Apologies for the slight delay — please find the requested materials attached.

Summary / short answers:
- Support coverage: Redwood provides 24/7 triage with an initial P1 response target of 1 hour. We have attached the on-call roster and the sla-support-window-matrix.csv showing coverage across PST/UTC/EET. For the marketplace listing we recommend the following sentence: "24/7 triage with 1-hour initial response for critical incidents; follow-up remediation timelines vary by issue complexity and are covered in contractual SOW." This gives clear, region-agnostic coverage while preventing overcommitment.

- 99.99% availability & "enterprise-grade reliability": That figure is a marketing-stated availability target measured over a rolling 30-day window; it is not a contractual SLA in the public listing. We agree with keeping the listing copy to the phrasing above and removing an unconditional "99.99%" claim from the marketplace listing unless the customer contract explicitly includes that SLA.

Attachments included: acme_evidence_matrix.xlsx (evidence map), sla-support-window-matrix.csv (coverage table), marketplace_banner_v4.png (artwork).

Next steps: if Azure Marketplace Compliance needs any specific supporting docs (SOC2 section pointers, sample support runbook excerpt), Ben can upload those to the Drive link.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
